back: The minimum energy required by an electron to escape from a metal surface. Denoted phi0, measured in eV (1 eV = 1.602 x 10^-19 J). Depends on the metal and on the nature of its surface.

front: Three ways to make a metal emit electrons
back: 1. Thermionic emission - by heating, so thermal energy lifts the electrons out. 2. Field emission - by a very strong electric field of order 10^8 V/m, as in a spark plug. 3. Photoelectric emission - by light of suitable frequency; the electrons are called photoelectrons.

The emission of electrons from a metal surface when it is illuminated by light of suitable frequency. Zinc, cadmium and magnesium respond only to ultraviolet; alkali metals (Li, Na, K, Cs, Rb) respond to visible light.
The minimum frequency nu0 below which no photoelectric emission occurs, however intense the light. It depends on the material of the emitter. nu0 = phi0/h.
The maximum photocurrent, reached when the accelerating potential is large enough that every emitted photoelectron reaches the collector. It is proportional to the intensity of the incident light.

The minimum negative potential V0 on the collector for which the photocurrent becomes zero. It just stops even the most energetic photoelectrons, so K_max = e V0. It depends on frequency and material, never on intensity.

front: Effect of intensity at fixed frequency
back: Photocurrent (and saturation current) is directly proportional to intensity - more photons, more electrons. The stopping potential and K_max are unchanged. Intensity fixes the number of electrons, not their energy.

front: Effect of frequency at fixed intensity
back: The saturation current stays about the same; the stopping potential becomes more negative as frequency rises, in the order V03 > V02 > V01 for nu3 > nu2 > nu1. Frequency fixes the energy of each electron.

K_max = h nu - phi0, where h nu is the energy of the absorbed quantum and phi0 the work function. It is conservation of energy for one photon absorbed by one electron. More tightly bound electrons emerge with less than K_max.

front: Einstein's equation as a straight line
back: e V0 = h nu - phi0, so V0 = (h/e) nu - phi0/e. The V0 against nu graph is a straight line of slope h/e, the same for all materials; the V0 intercept is -phi0/e and the nu intercept is nu0.

It assumes continuous absorption over the whole wavefront, so it predicts that K_max should grow with intensity, that no threshold frequency should exist, and that emission should take hours. All three are contradicted by experiment.

1. Radiation behaves as particles called photons. 2. Each photon has energy h nu and momentum h nu/c. 3. All photons of a given frequency have the same energy whatever the intensity. 4. Photons are electrically neutral, undeflected by E and B fields. 5. In a photon-particle collision total energy and momentum are conserved, but the number of photons need not be.
E = h nu = hc/lambda and p = h nu/c = h/lambda. Photon energy is independent of intensity; intensity only fixes how many photons arrive per second.
hc is about 1240 eV nm. So a photon of wavelength lambda nm carries about 1240/lambda eV. Example: 500 nm gives about 2.5 eV.

Between 1906 and 1916 Millikan tried to disprove Einstein's photoelectric equation. He measured the slope of the V0 against nu line, obtained h close to 6.626 x 10^-34 J s, and thereby proved the equation valid. Nobel Prize 1923. Einstein got the 1921 Nobel Prize for the photoelectric effect.

Moving particles of matter should display wave-like properties under suitable conditions, with wavelength lambda = h/p = h/(m v). De Broglie reasoned from the symmetry of nature: if radiation has a dual character, so should matter.
In lambda = h/p the left side is a wave attribute and the right side a particle attribute; Planck's constant h links the two. That is the whole dual nature of matter contained in a single relation.

front: de Broglie wavelength of a photon
back: For a photon p = h nu/c, so lambda = h/p = hc/(h nu) = c/nu - exactly the wavelength of the radiation whose quantum it is. The de Broglie relation therefore passes the photon test.

front: Orders of magnitude for matter waves
back: Electron at 5.4 x 10^6 m/s: lambda = 0.135 nm, comparable with X-rays and with atomic spacings. A 150 g ball at 30 m/s: lambda = 1.47 x 10^-34 m, about 10^-19 times a proton - unmeasurable.

front: Where the wave nature of matter shows
back: Only where the momentum is small: electrons, protons and other sub-atomic particles. Their de Broglie wavelength is of the order of the spacing between atomic planes in crystals, hence measurable. It is independent of the charge of the particle.

The nature of the experiment decides. Interference, diffraction and polarisation need the wave picture; photoelectric and Compton effects, which involve energy and momentum transfer, need the photon picture. In vision, the eye-lens needs waves and the retina needs photons.
In 1924 Compton scattered X-rays from electrons and found the photon handing over definite energy and momentum like a particle. This further confirmed the particle nature of light.

1. Photocurrent is proportional to intensity. 2. Saturation current is proportional to intensity while V0 is independent of it. 3. Below nu0 no emission at all; above nu0, V0 rises linearly with frequency. 4. Emission is instantaneous, within about 10^-9 s.
